mappings.note: Meaning of 'assertive'. Chapter vocabulary about how marginalised groups claim rights; no LO defines it, so goal-level rather than LO-43, which is about specific groups' rights.
Who wrote the poem on untouchability -> LO-43, which names Scheduled Castes among the groups whose rights are discussed.
Kabir's caste; a Bhakti voice against caste hierarchy -> LO-43.
Who faces inequality through marginalisation; identifying the affected groups -> LO-43, not the goal, because named groups are the answer.
Where Chokhamela was from; a Dalit Bhakti poet -> LO-43.
How government ends inequity (laws and policies); the protection and promotion half of LO-42, applied rather than group-specific.
The word for excluding or banishing a group (ostracise); vocabulary -> goal-level.
The word for expressing one's views strongly (assertive) -> goal-level, as with qid:111083.
The form Kabir wrote in; part of the Dalit and anti-caste literary tradition -> LO-43.
What manual scavenging is -> LO-43, which names sanitation workers explicitly.
When the Supreme Court banned manual scavenging. LO-44 covers writing about judges' role in delivering justice, which a date recall is not, so the sanitation-workers outcome is cited.
Article 15 barring discrimination on religion, race, caste, sex or birthplace -> LO-38, illustrating a Fundamental Right, rather than LO-43's group discussion.
Definition of a policy; chapter vocabulary -> goal-level.
The Act undoing injustice to forest dwellers (Forest Rights Act) -> LO-43, Scheduled Tribes.
What the 2006 Act did; the same Forest Rights Act -> LO-43.
Which Act matters for Adivasis -> LO-43.
Whom reservation policy benefits -> LO-43, which names Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The term meaning 'broken' (Dalit) -> LO-43.
Year of the 1993 dry latrines prohibition Act -> LO-43, sanitation workers.
Where Shakti and Tantric traditions came from; Adivasi influence on mainstream religion -> LO-43.
Whose poetry Dalits across several states still sing (Kabir) -> LO-43.
The name for forest-dwelling tribal people -> LO-43, Scheduled Tribes.
Who must keep working for equality and dignity; the promotion half of LO-42, stated generally rather than for a named group.
Whose students get free or subsidised hostels -> LO-43, Scheduled Castes and Tribes.
Who may claim reservation in government jobs -> LO-43.
Interval of the Jakmalgur deity festival; a detail of the case study about a Dalit priest refusing a demeaning ritual -> LO-43.
Number of priests at the Jakmalgur event; the same case study -> LO-43.
Who refused the foot-washing ritual; the central act of caste assertion in the case study -> LO-43.
Year of the SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act -> LO-43, which names both groups.
Who mainly does manual scavenging (Dalits) -> LO-43, sanitation workers and Scheduled Castes.
State where the Safai Karamchari Andolan began -> LO-43, sanitation workers organising for their rights.
Number of Dalits working as manual scavengers -> LO-43.
Daily earnings of municipal manual scavengers -> LO-43.
When the 2013 manual scavenging prohibition and rehabilitation Act took effect -> LO-43.
Naming an Adivasi activist -> LO-43, Scheduled Tribes asserting their rights.
